title: Layer 2 scaling solutions see unprecedented adoption rates
content:
TL;DR: The Bitcoin network continues its mission as the hardest money, with its base layer secured by a robust hashrate, even as Layer 2 solutions like Lightning see unprecedented adoption, enhancing its utility for global transactors. This scaling without compromise reinforces Bitcoin's unique role as the foundation of sovereign finance, demanding that informed users understand both its foundational security and its evolving transaction layers for optimal engagement. Prepare for an upcoming difficulty adjustment that will calibrate the network's computational challenge to current mining realities.

The Report

As of February 02, 2026, at 04:09 UTC, the Bitcoin network continues to operate with its characteristic precision and resilience, currently sitting at block height 934,678. The computational integrity of the network, the bedrock of its monetary sovereignty, is currently secured by a formidable hashrate of 853.02 exahashes per second (EH/s). While this figure represents a massive global effort to validate transactions and secure the ledger, it is important to note that it stands below the approximate 977 EH/s observed in late January 2026, and certainly below the peak readings of around 1042 EH/s seen in previous periods. This fluctuation is a natural part of the network's dynamic equilibrium, reflecting the ebb and flow of miner participation and economic incentives.

The network's self-regulating mechanism for security, the difficulty adjustment, is currently 63.0% complete, with approximately 746 blocks remaining until the next recalibration. The current difficulty, last adjusted on January 23, 2026, stands at 146.47 terahashes (T), which, crucially, is not an all-time high, remaining below the November 2025 peak of 155
